subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: On normal gateway SIGTERM/SIGINT, should OpenClaw cancel managed active/background exec child processes before the shutdown watchdog, preserve yielded/background work, or defer this behavior to a separate session/process control surface?
rationale: Current tests intentionally preserve active runs on normal shutdown, while resolving this report likely requires changing that lifecycle contract or adding a bounded exception path for managed child processes.

options.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
options.body: Normal stop would reject new work, drain briefly, then cancel managed exec/process scopes before the watchdog while documenting explicit preservation exceptions.

options.title: Preserve background exec on normal stop
options.body: OpenClaw would keep the current contract and improve diagnostics for the responsible child process when shutdown times out.

options.title: Defer to session kill design
options.body: This issue would wait for the broader session/process list-and-kill surface tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12554.

recommendation.title: Define bounded managed-process shutdown
recommendation.body: Normal stop would reject new work, drain briefly, then cancel managed exec/process scopes before the watchdog while documenting explicit preservation exceptions.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is a core lifecycle/product contract choice, and recent gateway lifecycle history points to steipete as the best available routing candidate.
